h1:
Roi Et Cafes
10 Spots Around Bueng Phlan Chai
intro: Bueng Phlan Chai is the heart of Roi Et town. After a loop around the lake you'll probably want somewhere to sit, sip a coffee and grab a few photos — and the area around the lake and in town has more cafes than you'd expect, from lakeside spots looking out at the Ho Huad tower to roasters who roast their own beans and small, prettily decorated shops. We've picked 10 that are genuinely open right now, with opening hours and rough prices so it's easier to plan.

blocks.html: Roi Et isn't just the Ho Huad tower and a stroll around Bueng Phlan Chai — the town's cafe scene has been growing steadily, with several spots opening in the last couple of years. Some make the most of the lakeside view, some focus on roasting their own beans, and some lean into photo-worthy corners that pull in a steady stream of check-ins. The handy part is that almost all of them sit in town, just a few minutes by car or motorbike taxi from the lake.

We ranked these from real reviews by people who've actually sat down, plus how convenient they are if you're starting from Bueng Phlan Chai. The top spots are easy to reach, have a good view and get talked about a lot, while the ones lower down are backups for when the first choice is packed or you fancy a change of scene.

blocks.text: 10 Roi Et cafes, from lakeside into town

items.name: SAO CAFE (Chao Cafe, lakeside)
items.blurb: A three-storey cafe right on Bueng Phlan Chai, with the top floor looking straight out at the Ho Huad tower. The menu is almost overwhelming — coffee, tea, dim sum, all the way to full mains — so it's the kind of place families settle in for a long sit. Lots of seating, but weekend evenings get fairly busy.
items.meta: On Bueng Phlan Chai lakeside · Open daily 07:00–21:30

items.name: HER Studio
items.blurb: A bare-concrete loft-style spot on Bueng Phlan Chai with a raw, cool tone. The iced latte is the regular order, and the photo angle over the water is lovely from late afternoon into the evening. Better suited to quiet working than to big groups.
items.meta: Bueng Phlan Chai lakeside · Open daily 10:00–19:00

items.name: FENWAY Café
items.blurb: A minimalist cafe in town where the cakes are the draw — especially the Basque burnt cheesecake and a pudding that plenty of people pair with their coffee. The mood is calm and steady, made for quietly sipping coffee and eating cake. Not far from the lake, just a few minutes by car.
items.price: Coffee from ฿55 · Cake ฿75–95 a slice

items.name: Hom Coffee
items.blurb: A small minimalist shop in the middle of town that focuses on carefully selected beans. The talked-about orders are the Dirty Coffee and the matcha latte. If you like a quiet, fuss-free spot, it's an easy short stop before or after walking the lake.
items.meta: In town, near the sights · Open most days

items.name: Acraft Coffee Roaster
items.blurb: Worth a stop if you're serious about coffee — this place roasts its own beans fresh every day, so it suits anyone who wants to try a pour-over or take beans home. It feels more like a roastery than a photo cafe, but you walk away with coffee that takes flavour seriously.

items.name: white house cafe & Studio
items.blurb: A crisp all-white cafe that comes with a photo studio inside. The white room and warm-light corners are where people come to get their shots. The menu runs to coffee, croissants, scones and cake — good for photo people who want clean, easy-to-tone images.

items.name: The Cottage 101
items.blurb: Tucked down a small lane in town, decorated like an English cottage — warm and friendly, with prices easier on the wallet than many spots. It's pet-friendly too, so you can bring your dog. Good for a long, unhurried sit.

items.name: Bonsai Cafe
items.blurb: A Japanese-toned cafe in town leaning on green tea and cake, with a calm mood and zen-ish photo corners at friendly prices. One thing to know: it's closed on Wednesdays, so if you're going midweek, check the day first.

items.name: Afternoon Bar & Bistro
items.blurb: A spot that works for daytime coffee and an evening bar mood, with a lawn area to relax on. The menu covers coffee, tea and bakery — good for a group of friends who want to carry on from afternoon into the evening.
items.meta: In town · Open afternoon to evening

items.name: RIMMM Coffee & Space
items.blurb: A riverside cafe built around a natural view and plenty of space, with a wide range of drinks. Good for escaping the busier in-town shops to sit quietly in the breeze. Easiest if you have your own transport.
items.meta: Riverside near town · Open most days

blocks.title: Tip on timing your visit
blocks.html: Lakeside spots like SAO CAFE and HER Studio look their best from late afternoon into the evening, when you get soft light and the view over the water — but that's also when they're busiest. If you want a clear photo angle, try a weekday late morning instead.

blocks.text: Pick a cafe by the vibe you're after

items.name: For the lakeside view
items.blurb: Want water and the Ho Huad tower as your backdrop? Go for SAO CAFE or HER Studio, both right on Bueng Phlan Chai and walkable from the lake.

items.name: For serious coffee
items.blurb: More about the coffee than the setting — head to Acraft Coffee Roaster, which roasts in-house, or Hom Coffee with its well-chosen beans.

items.name: For photos
items.blurb: Want clean, well-toned shots? Try the all-white white house cafe or the Japanese-style Bonsai Cafe — both fun for collecting angles.

items.name: For budget, long sits
items.blurb: Want to linger without spending much? The Cottage 101 and Bonsai Cafe have friendly prices and an easygoing mood.

blocks.text: Starting from Bueng Phlan Chai, which cafes are closest

blocks.html: The nice thing about Roi Et's cafes is that they cluster in town. Starting from Bueng Phlan Chai, lakeside spots like SAO CAFE and HER Studio are walkable or a few minutes by motorbike taxi, while in-town shops like FENWAY, Hom Coffee and white house are around a 5–10 minute drive away. That makes it easy to walk the lake in the morning and follow up with a cafe later on.

items: Walkable / a few minutes by motorbike taxi — SAO CAFE, HER Studio (right on Bueng Phlan Chai)
5–10 minute drive — FENWAY Café, Hom Coffee, Acraft Coffee Roaster, white house cafe
Easier with your own transport — RIMMM Coffee & Space, Afternoon Bar & Bistro (on the edge of town)

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: Several of these opened recently, so hours and menus can shift. If you're set on one particular spot, check its page before you head out to be sure — especially shops that close certain days, like Bonsai Cafe (closed Wednesdays).

faq.q: Which Roi Et cafes are actually right on Bueng Phlan Chai?
faq.a: The most talked-about spots right on the lakeside are SAO CAFE (Chao Cafe, lakeside), a three-storey shop looking out at the Ho Huad tower, and HER Studio, a loft-style spot by the water. Both are just a few minutes from the lake on foot or by motorbike taxi.

faq.q: Where should I go for serious coffee?
faq.a: If you care about the coffee more than the setting, go for Acraft Coffee Roaster, which roasts its own beans fresh every day and sells beans to take home, or Hom Coffee, with well-chosen beans and orders like the Dirty Coffee.

faq.q: Roughly how much do Roi Et cafes cost?
faq.a: Most drinks start around ฿50–80. Easier-on-the-wallet spots like The Cottage 101 or Bonsai Cafe start around ฿50–65, while lakeside cafes and ones with special cakes run a bit higher.

faq.q: When's the best time for cafe photos in Roi Et?
faq.a: Lakeside spots look best from late afternoon into the evening, when you get soft light and the view over the water — but that's also when they're busiest. For a clearer angle, try a weekday late morning. All-white spots like white house cafe photograph well all day since the light is controlled indoors.

faq.q: Are there any pet-friendly cafes in Roi Et?
faq.a: Yes — The Cottage 101 is an English-cottage-style spot down a small lane in town that's pet-friendly, so you can bring your dog along. The mood is warm and friendly.
